Lifecycle.QualityHelp: Compares the immutable Host quality snapshot for this game tick only when a Signal arrives. Exactly one branch executes. Missing quality returns NotReady; unknown or unsupported quality is an explicit error. No default tier is inferred.
Lifecycle.SignalCaptureHelp: Captures four finite, unitless user-defined numbers on each arrival. Wire its value to downstream inputs and its Signal to their execution path. Per-arrival owned snapshots survive FIFO branches; no engine object or pointer is retained. Use explicit conversions/Break for scalar, normal or color semantics. This is same-instance Signal context, not a cross-instance or asynchronous message.
Lifecycle.PresetDescription: One instance, three lazy phases. Start completes by time; Loop completes by count or the next boundary after a Loop-only End Request. End Complete does not destroy. Clone this group to change its policy; for immediate End, wire a separate unguarded Enter End. Reset the instance to replay this single-pass preset.
Lifecycle.PresetUnits: Seconds; whole loop intervals; limit flag 0 or 1
Lifecycle.PresetInputs: Start/Loop/End lengths, count, limit flag, Loop-only End Request
Lifecycle.PresetOutputs: Active interval data (time/index/boundaries/complete), phase time, End Complete
Lifecycle.PresetState: Instance-owned phase and clocks; no implicit Life Time, random or child reset
Lifecycle.LoopLengthHelp: Seconds per interval; zero is supported only with a bounded count.
Lifecycle.LoopCountHelp: Nonnegative whole intervals, captured at Loop entry.
Lifecycle.LimitCountHelp: Checked: finish after the count. Unchecked: wait for an external request during Loop.
Lifecycle.EndLengthHelp: Seconds until End Complete; does not determine Life Time or destruction.
Lifecycle.LoopClockHelp: Connect Phase Time for a phase-local loop, or leave Time at -1 for instance age. Break the Vector4 into interval time, zero-based index, cumulative boundaries and completion. Long jumps emit one boundary signal with the cumulative count. Arm waits for a strictly later boundary; a completed clock cannot arm. Reset captures the interval/count inputs again. No Life Time or destruction is inferred.
Lifecycle.PhaseHelp: One phase per instance. Entering even the same phase restarts its clock at the request time; selection changes at the next evaluation boundary. State, random streams, children and Life Time are preserved. End does not destroy the instance. Use the LifecyclePhase Enum Select to skip inactive parameter and Signal branches.
Lifecycle.ForceCurrentHelp: Interrupt this Spawnable instance, or the whole effect at its root. Discards pending signals and rendering without End or natural Destroy.
Lifecycle.ForceEffectHelp: Interrupt the whole effect and all its generated instances. Does not run End or natural Destroy; the host releases rendering at the completed job boundary.
